name: MCCompiled
description: production-ready programming language that compiles to minecraft bedrock commands.

sections.WHAT: MCCompiled is a DSL that, rather than compile to instructions or any sort of IL, compiles to Minecraft: Bedrock Edition function files. Function files are collections of commands that are run sequentially, presenting a rather unique challenge as a compile-target.
sections.WHY: I work part-time as an addons/commands developer for Lifeboat Network's marketplace team. Developing large, sustainable projects with complex logic just wasn't possible, so I began this project on the side to help speed up my work. I open-sourced it and released it to the Bedrock community after over 18 months of work.
sections.PARADIGM: Generally, MCCompiled operates as any traditional procedural programming language, similarly to C. Minecraft doesn't inherently have scope or even blocks, so code flow is boiled down to a little more than jumping in and out of subroutines. These limitations are almost completely abstracted away by MCCompiled. (although you still need a bit of knowledge about Minecraft Commands to use it effectively and understand the limitations).
sections.IDE: MCCompiled also has an IDE based entirely inside a web-app, supporting easy file i/o, live code linting, symbol information, and compilation straight into development folders. It works using protocol URLs and a local websocket server to process the code. There's also good developer documentation with the support for other devs to develop software on top of this server.
sections.WHAT I GAINED: Ironically, I ended up spending more time working on this project than I probably would have just done projects with raw commands, but... I learned to write a whole freaking compiler, with optimizations, control flow, async, inline operations, and so much more! I got to collaborate with a community member to integrate with a popular tool runner, learned about web standards for my IDE (and am actively working on implementing LSP), and limped my way through this unrealistically difficult project. I've made a lot of cool personal projects over the years, but nine times out of ten I'd consider this my magnum opus.
